LESSON: READING 7.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: VISUALS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.2: Reading 7.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visuals
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 7.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visuals, part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: What information do we obtain from visuals? 2. How can one interpret a visual correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify different visuals in given contexts correctly,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 7.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visuals in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. make a connection between visuals and the written text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 7.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visuals in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. interpret visuals correctly for meaning,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 7.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visuals in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the role of visuals in simplifying representation. • Study information presented in optical illusions in print/ electronic devices and discuss findings, Adjust light intensity when using the digital device for learners with visual difficulties. • Make inference of implied meaning from the visuals, Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication 1. What information do we obtain from visuals? 2. How can one interpret a visual correctly? 61 modes as they share their views. • Work with peers to make connections of the visuals such as pictures, graphs, illustrations, charts and videos provided with written texts, • Write a summary of what has been viewed in the visuals which may depict human- wildlife conflict, Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing materials or type on appropriate adapted digital devices to write the summary. • Present a piece of written information on wildlife in form of a visual and share in class. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use any functional part of the body or use appropriate assistive devices during presentations. 62

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 7.2.1 Intensive Reading: Visuals together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Citizenship is fostered as the learner interacts with information from various visual materials on human wildlife conflict.

• Learning to learn is enhanced as the learner works independently to make visuals in line with the theme of wildlife.

Values:
Patriotism is promoted as the learner acquires knowledge on his or her environment while reading about the importance of

wildlife.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Environmental and social issues are promoted as the learner learns the importance of co-existing with wildlife.

Link to other subjects:

The learner is able to relate visuals as an aspect of learning in Pre- technical Studies

Main points to remember:

1. identify different visuals in given contexts correctly,
2. make a connection between visuals and the written text,
3. interpret visuals correctly for meaning,

Learners with manipulation difficulties could use any functional part of the body or use appropriate assistive devices during presentations. 62
